rows.grounds: ablative indicating occasion or incidental context
locative adverb referring to the present discussion
fused form of tasya and api, referring back to mantra
essential nature or intrinsic form
being taught or established in the text

items.question: What justifies expounding the essential nature of mantra incidentally in this context?
premises: The discussion has reached a relevant contextual occasion.
The nature of mantra is connected to the preceding topic.
An incidental exposition can still establish essential nature.
items.inference: Therefore, the essential nature of mantra is appropriately expounded here by contextual connection.
uncertainties: The exact antecedent of tasyāpi is inferred from context as mantra.
items.plain_english: Incidentally in this context, the essential nature of that as well is expounded.

rows.grounds: instrumental compound expressing protection through self-reflective awareness
saving or protecting function
regarded or desired as the defining characteristic
defining mark of mantra

items.question: What defining characteristic constitutes the essential nature of mantra?
premises: Mantra is characterized by a specific function.
Protection arises through one's own reflective awareness.
This protective function is accepted as mantra's defining mark.
items.inference: Therefore, protection through one's own reflective nature is the defining characteristic of mantra.
items.plain_english: Protection through one's own reflective nature is accepted as the defining characteristic of mantra.

rows.grounds: demonstrative referring to the two aspects just stated
the twofold nature or dual aspect
having pervasion as its core essence
manifestly or distinctly
as directly evident in experience
standing or present as a fact

items.question: How is the twofold nature of mantra established in direct experience?
premises: Mantra has a twofold nature.
This pair has pervasion as its essence.
It is clearly present in direct perception.
items.inference: Therefore, the twofold nature of mantra, essentially pervading, is clearly established in direct experience.
uncertainties: The exact two members of the pair are understood from the preceding verse.
items.plain_english: This pair, whose essence is pervasion, is clearly established as directly perceptible.

rows.grounds: instrumental-ablative compound indicating power arising from complete knowledge
worldly becoming or conditioned existence
turns into or comes to be
the very ground or basis of liberation

items.question: What transformative effect does thorough knowledge of this mantra nature produce?
premises: Thorough knowledge of this nature has a decisive power.
Conditioned existence is ordinarily a state of bondage.
Knowledge can transform the status of existence.
items.inference: Therefore, by thorough knowledge of this, conditioned existence becomes the ground of liberation.
items.plain_english: By the power of thoroughly knowing this, worldly existence becomes the ground of liberation.

rows.grounds: in an undivided or non-differentiated manner
operate or remain present
in all domains or levels of experience

items.question: How do these principles operate across all domains of experience?
premises: Experience occurs in multiple domains or grounds.
The operative principles are not confined to one domain.
They function without internal division.
items.inference: Therefore, they abide without division in all grounds of experience.
uncertainties: The subject of vartante is implied from the preceding context.
items.plain_english: They abide without division in all grounds of experience.

rows.grounds: name of the mudrā, moving in the void
connective particle
marker indicating designation
of the seal or gesture
through having a fivefold constitution
mode of being or established condition

items.question: What constitutes the established state of the mudrā known as khecarī?
premises: Khecarī is identified as a specific mudrā.
A mudrā can have a structured constitution.
Its state is determined by a fivefold nature.
items.inference: Therefore, the state of the mudrā called khecarī consists in its fivefold nature.
items.plain_english: And the state of the mudrā called khecarī is established through its fivefold nature.

rows.grounds: ordered progression
referring to the previously mentioned state or structure
in corresponding numerical order
by means of these elements or aspects
pervasive connection in every respect

items.question: How does the sequence of that fivefold state relate to all its aspects?
premises: The fivefold state has an internal sequence.
Its elements correspond in numerical order.
These elements are connected in every respect.
items.inference: Therefore, its sequence corresponds in order and is connected with these in all ways.
uncertainties: The referent of etābhiḥ is taken as the fivefold aspects from the prior verse.
items.plain_english: Its sequence, in corresponding order, is connected with these in every way.

rows.grounds: through inseparable mutual concomitance
from perfect sameness of essence or taste
state of being undivided or identical

items.question: What establishes the non-difference among these mutually related aspects?
premises: The aspects do not deviate from one another.
They share a sameness of essence.
Mutual inseparability and shared essence imply non-difference.
items.inference: Therefore, by mutual non-deviation and sameness of essence, there is non-difference.
items.plain_english: Through their mutual non-deviation and sameness of essence, there is non-difference.

rows.grounds: by the power arising from complete knowledge of that
that which is based in body, speech, and mind

items.question: What domain is transformed through thorough knowledge of this non-difference?
premises: Thorough knowledge has transformative power.
Human functioning rests on body, speech, and mind.
This domain is subject to the knowledge described.
items.inference: Therefore, by thorough knowledge of this, what rests on body, speech, and mind is transformed.
uncertainties: The predicate completing this clause continues in the following verse.
items.plain_english: By the power of thoroughly knowing this, that which rests on body, speech, and mind...

rows.grounds: the state of pervading the triad of absorptions beginning with āṇava

items.question: What realized state encompasses the triad of absorptions beginning with the individual?
premises: There is a triad of absorptions beginning with āṇava.
A higher realization can pervade this triad.
This pervading form is the result indicated by prior knowledge.
items.inference: Therefore, the result is the pervading form of the triad of absorptions beginning with āṇava.
uncertainties: This verse functions as the completion of the clause begun in verse 396.
items.plain_english: ...attains the form that pervades the triad of absorptions beginning with the āṇava.

rows.grounds: the three impurities associated with yādi, karma, and so on
without step-by-step order
merging or dissolution into a higher state

items.question: How does the triad of impurities undergo dissolution in this realization?
premises: A triad of impurities is present as a limiting condition.
Dissolution can occur in realization.
This dissolution does not follow a sequential order.
items.inference: Therefore, the triad of impurities undergoes dissolution non-sequentially.
uncertainties: The exact mapping of yādi and karma to specific impurities is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: The triad of impurities beginning with yādi and karma dissolves non-sequentially.

rows.grounds: through the bringing forth or projection of will
emanated or brought into manifestation
starting from the level of kālāgni
extending as far as the level of śiva

items.question: What range of manifestation arises from the emission of will?
premises: Will can emit or project manifestation.
Manifestation spans a graded range of levels.
This range extends from kālāgni up to śiva.
items.inference: Therefore, from the emission of will, what is created extends from kālāgni up to śiva.
uncertainties: ākālāgni is read as indicating the lower limit beginning with kālāgni.
items.plain_english: From the emission of will, creation extends from kālāgni up to śiva.
